answer: Require every agent to bind its identity to a single costly cipher credential: a key pair created through a verifiable, resource-intensive ceremony and tied to one device or deposit, so an attacker cannot forge thousands of identities for free. A lightweight sparrow agent can still join with a small credential and limited rights, earning more trust only through a history of verified work. Peers check signatures and past behaviour before accepting transactions, so cloning an identity means redoing the costly ceremony each time, making large-scale sybil creation uneconomical.
